title: Security Engineering, Zero-Trust Architecture & SPIFFE/SPIRE Workload Identity
summary: Master cloud-native security engineering and Zero-Trust architecture: implementing cryptographic workload identity with SPIFFE/SPIRE (spiffe://), IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA) federation, kernel-level eBPF runtime security tracing with Cilium Tetragon, in-kernel syscall filtering (sys_execve), and automated zero-trust egress posture.
learningObjectives: Architect zero-trust cryptographic workload identity using SPIFFE/SPIRE SVID federation and AWS IAM Roles for Service Accounts (IRSA).
Configure kernel-level eBPF runtime execution policies with Cilium Tetragon to detect and block unauthorized binaries and syscall execution.
Implement defense-in-depth zero-trust security postures eliminating static shared credentials across multi-tenant microservices.

curriculumModules.title: Cryptographic Workload Identity, SPIFFE/SPIRE & Cloud IAM Federation
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Zero-trust architecture rejects network-perimeter security in favor of verifiable cryptographic identity. The Secure Production Identity Framework for Everyone (SPIFFE) defines standard SPIFFE IDs (spiffe://<trust-domain>/ns/<namespace>/sa/<serviceaccount>) and X.509 SVID credentials issued dynamically by SPIRE agents. Combined with cloud IAM federation (such as AWS IRSA / EKS Pod Identity), Kubernetes ServiceAccounts assume cloud IAM roles via OpenID Connect (OIDC) tokens, eliminating long-lived static API secrets.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Federate short-lived SPIFFE SVIDs and AWS IRSA annotations to authenticate microservices dynamically against cloud databases and external vaults without hardcoded keys.

curriculumModules.title: Kernel-Level eBPF Runtime Security & Cilium Tetragon Tracing Policies
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Traditional runtime security agents relying on ptrace or userspace auditd hooks impose high CPU overhead and suffer from race conditions (TOCTOU). Cilium Tetragon executes directly inside Linux kernel eBPF probes (kprobes, tracepoints, LSM hooks) to intercept system calls like sys_execve, sys_socket, and sys_open before execution finishes. Tetragon TracingPolicy manifests enforce in-kernel process termination (SIGKILL) when unauthorized binaries (such as netcat, nmap, or curl) execute inside high-security containers.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Deploy declarative Cilium Tetragon TracingPolicy CRDs enforcing kernel-level sys_execve syscall filtering to block interactive reverse-shell utilities in production pods.

labs.scenario: Configure zero-trust cryptographic workload identity for the payment service. Author a SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity ConfigMap in /security/spiffe-workload-identity.yaml named spiffe-workload-identity in namespace production with data keys: trustDomain: 'prod.kubelabs.io', spiffeId: 'spiffe://prod.kubelabs.io/ns/production/sa/payment-service-sa', and svidTtlMinutes: '60'. Apply both manifests to namespace production.

labs.title: Kernel-Level eBPF Runtime Security Policy with Cilium Tetragon
labs.scenario: Enforce real-time kernel-level runtime protection against reverse shells. Author manifest /security/tetragon-policy.yaml containing a Cilium TracingPolicy named block-unauthorized-binaries in namespace production. Configure spec.kprobes with call: sys_execve, syscall: true, and an action: Sigkill on matching binaries /bin/netcat and /usr/bin/nc. Next, deploy a Deployment named secure-vault-client in namespace production running 2 replicas with image vault-client:v1.0. Apply both manifests to namespace production.
labs.productionContext: eBPF Tetragon operates inside Linux kernel tracepoints and kprobes, providing sub-millisecond in-kernel process termination (Sigkill) on unauthorized execution attempts without depending on slow userspace log scrapers.
objectives: Create namespace production if not present.
Author manifest /security/tetragon-policy.yaml defining TracingPolicy block-unauthorized-binaries and Deployment secure-vault-client.
Configure TracingPolicy to intercept sys_execve with Sigkill.
Deploy secure-vault-client with 2 replicas in namespace production.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: cilium.io/v1alpha1
kind: TracingPolicy
metadata:
  name: block-unauthorized-binaries
  namespace: production
spec:
  kprobes:
    - call: "sys_execve"
      syscall: true
      args:
        - index: 0
          type: "string"
      selectors:
        - matchArgs:
            - index: 0
              operator: "In"
              values:
                - "/bin/netcat"
                - "/usr/bin/nc"
          matchActions:
            - action: "Sigkill"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-vault-client
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure-vault-client
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secure-vault-client
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: client
          image: vault-client:v1.0

steps.title: Create production namespace
steps.instruction: Create namespace production if not present.

steps.title: Author Tetragon TracingPolicy and Deployment
steps.instruction: Author manifest /security/tetragon-policy.yaml defining TracingPolicy block-unauthorized-binaries and Deployment secure-vault-client.

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /security/tetragon-policy.yaml
apiVersion: cilium.io/v1alpha1
kind: TracingPolicy
metadata:
  name: block-unauthorized-binaries
  namespace: production
spec:
  kprobes:
    - call: "sys_execve"
      syscall: true
      args:
        - index: 0
          type: "string"
      selectors:
        - matchArgs:
            - index: 0
              operator: "In"
              values:
                - "/bin/netcat"
                - "/usr/bin/nc"
          matchActions:
            - action: "Sigkill"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-vault-client
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure-vault-client
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secure-vault-client
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: client
          image: vault-client:v1.0
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.cause: TracingPolicy must target sys_execve with Sigkill, and Deployment must run 2 replicas.

assessmentQuestions.question: In a cloud-native Zero-Trust architecture, why is cryptographic SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity superior to static IAM access keys or bearer tokens?
options: SPIFFE SVIDs allow pods to bypass cluster network policies.

SPIFFE provides short-lived, automatically rotated, cryptographically signed X.509 or JWT identities issued dynamically based on verifiable platform attestation (node & pod metadata), eliminating persistent static credentials and enabling seamless cross-cloud/OIDC federation.
SPIFFE encrypts all Linux kernel binaries on the worker nodes.
SPIFFE completely disables DNS inside the Kubernetes cluster.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: SPIFFE/SPIRE eliminates static secrets by establishing short-lived, verifiable cryptographic SVIDs based on workload attestation, allowing automated mutual TLS and seamless cloud IAM role federation (such as AWS IRSA) without long-lived credentials.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does Cilium Tetragon eBPF-based runtime security achieve synchronous in-kernel enforcement compared to traditional userspace audit agents like Falco?
options: Tetragon pauses all cluster nodes for 10 seconds to analyze logs before resuming.

Tetragon instruments Linux kernel kprobes, tracepoints, and LSM hooks directly via eBPF bytecode, allowing it to inspect syscall arguments (such as sys_execve) and immediately terminate malicious processes (Sigkill) synchronously in kernel space before execution completes, preventing TOCTOU race conditions and user-space bypasses.
Tetragon runs exclusively as a browser extension on developer workstations.
Tetragon modifies the Linux kernel source code and reboots the server during every pod restart.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Because Tetragon runs via eBPF probes inside the kernel itself, it can enforce actions like Sigkill synchronously on syscall entry/exit, eliminating Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) windows and avoiding the CPU overhead of userspace context switching.
